來源未提供系統教材，可依所述演奏方式整理基本操作：取一根具彈性的長桿，兩端以緊繃: The source gives no systematic method, so the basic operation can be put together from the playing it describes: take a long, flexible rod with a taut string joining its two ends; the sound is usually made by plucking the string with the hand, though another bow may be drawn across it, or a thin stick may strike it. A musical bow usually has no built-in resonator, so a beginner can first practise plucking without one, then try fitting a resonator (a gourd, say) behind the stave, or taking one end partly into the mouth and using the mouth to change the size of the resonance so that overtones form a melody. Another point is the difference between the open and the stopped string: with the hand off the string you get the open note, and shortening or stopping the string with the hand gives another fundamental, the interval between the two being a whole tone, a semitone or a minor third.

樂弓屬311.1，音量偏弱，需靠口、葫蘆或地面凹坑共鳴。其最低、最強音為弦本身的: The musical bow is 311.1; its volume is weak and it needs the mouth, a gourd or a hollow in the ground to resonate. Its lowest and strongest note is the fundamental of the string itself, and the higher notes are overtones brought out by the resonator. It gives at least two fundamentals, open and stopped, most often a whole tone apart but sometimes a semitone or a minor third; some bows give three or four notes. The player plucks the string with the hand or a stick, or draws a second bow across it, and mouth resonance changes the size of the cavity so that the melody is made of notes resonated in the mouth. This sets it apart from the classical string instruments with a built-in soundbox.
樂弓屬弦鳴樂器，發聲體為一端至另一端張緊的弦，常見以木製彈性弓身搭配金屬弦；演奏: The musical bow is a chordophone whose sounding body is a string stretched from one end of the stave to the other, commonly a flexible wooden stave with a metal string; it may be plucked, rubbed or struck with the hand, a wooden bar or a twig. The resonator is usually a gourd fixed to the back of the stave, or else the mouth, a hollow in the ground or a bowl-shaped hollow object. Some regions use particular materials: the Cambodian kse diev uses a bronze string, the Indian malunga bamboo, a gut string and a coconut gourd, and the New Zealand ku a wooden stave and a fibre string. The sources state no materials for the remaining parts.
樂弓是否由獵弓發展而來仍不確定，但卡拉哈里沙漠的桑人或布希曼人會把獵弓轉作音樂用: Whether the musical bow developed from the hunting bow is still uncertain, but the San or Bushmen of the Kalahari do turn the hunting bow to musical use. Around 13,000 BCE Henri Breuil described a French cave image as a musical bow being blown, though the reading is unclear. Curt Sachs thought the hunting bow unlikely to be the musical bow, yet proposed that the musical bow may be the ancestor of the pierced lute. The key to its development is the resonator — a bowl, a gourd or the mouth; it moved from several notes on one string to one note per string, and from there to the bow harp, the harp and the lyre, with double stops and chords appearing. It is still found today in Eswatini, East Africa, Madagascar and Réunion, and in Brazil, Cambodia, India, Guam, Mauritius, the United States, Mexico, Zambia, Zimbabwe, New Zealand, Hawaii and Curaçao.
樂弓為弦鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs分類311.1，屬棒狀齊特爾類。: The musical bow is a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 311.1, in the class of bar zithers. It is a flexible wooden stave with a metal string stretched between its ends; it is played by plucking the string with the hand or a stick, with resonance from the mouth, the ground or a gourd. It is used by many African peoples and by Native Americans; in Africa it is often played by a soloist, and it also appears as the berimbau in the capoeira circle.
